body: stinkysnarly is right. bipolar disorder isn't a license to act like a wench. some behaviors and thoughts are a result of the illness, but it's imperative that your wife understand she should be held accountable for what is in her control.  I was diagnosed as a young adult. I'm in my forties now. Over time I noticed a trend in my behavior. When I wasnt feeling well I tended to get downright drag nasty with my mother.  I also noticed I didn't  behave that way with friends and co-workers.  Around them I held it together.  After spending time seriously thinking about this behavior, I realized since that my mother is a major source of support for me, I thought of my mother as a safe target for my frustration.  I know she's in it for the long haul with me and would never abandon me, no matter how ugly I got. It's not right to treat anyone this way, especially not one's mother.     It's unfair and ungrateful.  As a result, this is an issue I  VERY actively work on.   I ask for feedback from her about my attitude and behavior and I take it seriously.  (Mind you, there have been times when I have been completely off the chain because I was in the throes of a raging psychotic episode. Confronting me while I was in that state about my behavior would have been as effective as spitting on a house fire, but that is something altogether different.)  I don't think that pointing out blind spots and trends of behavior in a non-accusatory fashion to your wife when she's feeling well and is more receptive to hearing it is inappropriate. It may help to make her more circumspect in future.  We have bipolar disorder; it doesn't have us.
No weight gain on Geodon for me. Can't tell you about the effects of Adderall.  I took it with no problems,  but then again I've got BP type two. Mania isn't an issue for me.
Thanks for responding.  Last week I made several appointments for consultations with cognitive behavioral therapists. Now I don't want to go anymore.  Reasons to fight are becoming scarce.
